definitionEn: the process of working together with other people to produce or achieve something
situation: People or organisations join forces on a shared piece of work, such as research, an album or a product.

examples.text: The new range of trainers was designed in [[collaboration]] with a young fashion designer.
The discovery was the result of close [[collaboration]] between chemists and computer scientists.
The programme encourages [[collaboration]] between schools in different countries.

texts: The album was recorded in [[collaboration]] with a symphony orchestra.
Good [[collaboration]] between nurses and doctors saves lives.
The report stresses the need for international [[collaboration]] on climate.

badCollocation.noteRu: Стандартная фраза в объявлениях и письмах — thank you for your cooperation. Collaboration — совместная творческая или научная работа.

collocationTask.explanationRu: В тесном сотрудничестве с кем-то — in close collaboration with. Teamwork, unity и work в этой конструкции не используются.

nuance.text: The festival was organised in [[collaboration]] with local artists and schools.
nuance.explanationRu: Collaboration — открытая совместная работа. Collusion — тайный сговор ради нечестной цели, поэтому in collusion with local artists звучит как обвинение.

reverse.text: Two supermarket chains were fined for [[collusion]] over milk prices.
reverse.explanationRu: Незаконный сговор, например о ценах, — collusion. Collaboration — честная совместная работа, за неё не штрафуют.

fixIt.text: The new drug was developed through close [[co-working]] between scientists in Oslo and Madrid.
fixIt.explanationRu: Совместная работа учёных — collaboration. Co-working — это коворкинг, общее офисное пространство, а не сотрудничество.

wordFormation.text: Designing the new park was a truly [[collaborative]] effort involving local residents.

reply.context: At a job interview, you're asked: "How do you usually work with other departments?"
options: I prefer collaboration, so I usually do everything alone and just report at the end.
Collaboration? Yeah, whatever works, I'm easy.
I believe in close collaboration — regular check-ins and shared goals from day one.
reply.explanationRu: Collaboration — совместная работа, а не «всё делать в одиночку». Второй ответ слишком небрежный для собеседования.

rewrite.original: The museum and a local school worked together on the exhibition.
rewrite.frame: The museum organised the exhibition in ____ a local school.
rewrite.explanationRu: Совместно с кем-то — in collaboration with.

definitionEn: shared, done or felt by all the members of a group together
situation: Everyone in a team, community or country shares a decision, a responsibility, a memory or an effort.

examples.text: The failure of the project was a [[collective]] responsibility, not the fault of one manager.
Old photographs and songs help to keep a nation's [[collective]] memory alive.
Workers won better pay through [[collective]] action rather than individual complaints.

texts: We made a [[collective]] decision to cancel the trip.
When the results came in, there was a [[collective]] sigh of relief in the office.
The team celebrated its [[collective]] success with a dinner.

badCollocation.noteRu: Общее фото — a group photo. Collective говорят о решениях, ответственности и действиях: collective responsibility.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Все разом облегчённо выдохнули — a collective sigh of relief, устойчивое выражение. Rest, calm и comfort с sigh of не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The whole nation felt a [[collective]] sense of pride after the team's victory.
nuance.explanationRu: Collective — общий для всей большой группы: a collective sense of pride. Joint — совместный для нескольких конкретных участников: a joint account, a joint statement.

reverse.text: My partner and I opened a [[joint]] bank account after the wedding.
reverse.explanationRu: Общий счёт двух людей — a joint account. Collective говорят о целом коллективе или обществе, а не о паре.

fixIt.text: The union called for [[collected]] action to protect jobs at the factory.
fixIt.explanationRu: Совместные действия, например профсоюза, — collective action. Collected значит «собранный, спокойный» или «собранный в одном месте».

wordFormation.text: The five of us are [[collectively]] responsible for the budget.

reply.context: At a team meeting, your manager says: "The client is unhappy with the report. How did this happen?"
options: Honestly, it was a collective failure. We all rushed it, so we should all fix it.
It was a collective failure — Mark did the whole thing by himself.
Collective culpability is hereby acknowledged by the undersigned.
reply.explanationRu: Collective — общий для всей группы, поэтому «коллективная ошибка одного человека» — противоречие. Третий ответ звучит как юридический документ, а не ответ на встрече.

rewrite.original: Everyone in the team is responsible for the result.

definitionEn: an accident in which a moving vehicle, ship or person hits another
senseNote: Здесь — физическое столкновение; в переносном смысле — столкновение идей или интересов (a collision of cultures).
situation: Two cars, ships, planes or people crash into each other, usually by accident.

examples.text: Three people were injured in a [[collision]] between a bus and a lorry on the motorway.
The goalkeeper was taken to hospital after a [[collision]] with an opposing player.
Scientists believe the moon formed after a [[collision]] between the young Earth and another planet.

texts: The ship's radar should have prevented the [[collision]].
Luckily, nobody was hurt in the [[collision]] at the crossroads.
Two cyclists had a minor [[collision]] on the narrow path.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Конфликт интересов» — a conflict of interest; о споре мнений — a clash. Collision — прежде всего физическое столкновение.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Лобовое столкновение — a head-on collision (или head-on crash). Collapse — обрушение, contact — контакт, incident — происшествие; с head-on они не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The two ships were on a [[collision]] course until the captain changed direction.
nuance.explanationRu: On a collision course — на курсе, который ведёт к столкновению. Crash course — ускоренный интенсивный курс обучения, совсем другое значение.

reverse.text: Before the trip, I did a two-week [[crash]] course in Spanish.
reverse.explanationRu: Ускоренный курс обучения — crash course. Collision course — курс, ведущий к столкновению, к учёбе не относится.

fixIt.text: Nobody was hurt in this morning's [[clash]] between a taxi and a delivery van.
fixIt.explanationRu: Столкновение машин — collision (или crash). Clash — стычка между людьми или конфликт мнений, о ДТП так не говорят.

wordFormation.text: The pilot's quick reaction prevented a mid-air [[collision]].

reply.context: A friend texts: "Sorry I'm late — there's been an accident on the bridge and nothing's moving."
options: Please provide a full written account of the collision upon arrival.
Oh no, a collision! Was it a very long argument?
Oh no, I hope nobody was hurt in the collision. Take your time.
reply.explanationRu: Collision — физическое столкновение машин, а не спор. Первый ответ звучит как требование страховой компании, а не как ответ другу.

definitionEn: connected with the rule of one country over another land and its people
senseNote: Здесь — о колониальном правлении и его эпохе; в США colonial также называют архитектурный стиль XVII–XVIII веков.
situation: You talk about the time when a powerful country ruled another territory, or what that time left behind.

examples.text: Many of the region's roads and railways were built in the [[colonial]] era.
The country gained independence in 1962 after almost a century of [[colonial]] rule.
The old town is full of elegant [[colonial]] buildings with wooden balconies and shutters.

texts: The museum tells the story of the city's [[colonial]] past.
Spain and Portugal were major [[colonial]] powers in the sixteenth century.
The hotel is a beautiful [[colonial]] mansion surrounded by gardens.

badCollocation.noteRu: Территория под чужим управлением — a colony (a former British colony). Colonial — прилагательное: colonial rule, colonial buildings.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Под колониальным управлением — under colonial rule. Management и leadership — о руководстве компанией или командой, command — о военном командовании.

nuance.text: Many local languages were banned in schools during the [[colonial]] period.
nuance.explanationRu: Colonial — связанный с колониями и их управлением: так говорят о прошлом бывшей колонии. Imperial — связанный с империей или императором: an imperial palace, the imperial family.

reverse.text: Tourists queue for hours to visit the [[imperial]] palace.
reverse.explanationRu: Дворец императора — imperial palace. Colonial относится к колониям и колониальному правлению, а не к императорской семье.

fixIt.text: The port grew rich from the sugar trade during the [[colonist]] era.
fixIt.explanationRu: Нужно прилагательное: the colonial era — колониальная эпоха. Colonist — существительное, «колонист, поселенец».

wordFormation.text: Many streets in the capital still have their old [[colonial]] names.

rewrite.original: For two hundred years, the island was ruled by a European country.
rewrite.frame: For two hundred years, the island was under ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: Под управлением другой страны — under colonial rule.

definitionEn: a journalist who writes a regular opinion piece for a newspaper, magazine or website
situation: Someone writes a regular article in the same newspaper, sharing opinions about politics, food, money or life.

examples.text: As a food [[columnist]], she eats out four nights a week and writes about it every Sunday.
In this week's piece, the paper's political [[columnist]] criticises the new housing policy.
The magazine's advice [[columnist]] receives hundreds of letters about love and family problems every week.

texts: She started as a sports reporter and is now a weekly [[columnist]].
The [[columnist]] apologised for a joke that offended many readers.
Every newspaper needs a sharp [[columnist]] who isn't afraid to annoy people.

badCollocation.noteRu: Колумнист пишет колонки в газете, журнале или онлайн. На радио и ТВ обозревателя называют commentator или presenter.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Колумнист, который пишет о политике, — a political columnist: нужно прилагательное. Politician — политик, politic — «благоразумный», politically — наречие.

nuance.text: Every Saturday, the [[columnist]] shares her strong opinions on modern parenting.
nuance.explanationRu: Columnist — автор регулярной колонки, где главное — его мнение. Correspondent — корреспондент, который сообщает новости с места событий или по своей теме.

reverse.text: Our Tokyo [[correspondent]] sends this report from the scene of the earthquake.
reverse.explanationRu: Журналист, который передаёт новости с места событий, — correspondent. Columnist пишет авторские колонки с мнением, а не репортажи.

fixIt.text: She's the magazine's technology [[observer]] and writes a new piece every week.
fixIt.explanationRu: Автор регулярной колонки — columnist. Observer — наблюдатель (например, на выборах), журналистов-обозревателей так не называют.

wordFormation.text: After years as a reporter, he became a [[columnist]] with his own weekly page.

definitionEn: to take action to reduce or stop something harmful, such as crime or disease
senseNote: Здесь — «бороться с проблемой»; в прямом смысле combat — сражаться с противником, а существительное combat — «бой».
situation: Governments, doctors or companies take serious action against a problem like crime, disease, fraud or loneliness.

examples.text: The city has hired more police officers to [[combat]] rising street crime.
Doctors say regular exercise is one of the best ways of [[combating]] stress.
The council runs weekly lunches to [[combat]] loneliness among older residents.

texts: New laws are needed to [[combat]] the spread of fake news.
Scientists are developing new drugs to [[combat]] resistant bacteria.
The campaign aims to [[combat]] bullying in secondary schools.

badCollocation.noteRu: Combat — бороться против чего-то, без предлога: combat crime. «Бороться за» что-то — fight for: fight for equal rights.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Бороться с распространением — combat (или fight, tackle) the spread. Struggle и compete требуют предлога (with, against), а win значит «выиграть».

nuance.text: The city launched a campaign to [[combat]] litter in its parks.
nuance.explanationRu: Combat — активно бороться с проблемой, чтобы её стало меньше. Resist — сопротивляться давлению или соблазну (resist change, resist temptation); с мусором так не говорят.

reverse.text: I couldn't [[resist]] the temptation to have another slice of cake.
reverse.explanationRu: Не устоять перед соблазном — can't resist the temptation. Combat — бороться с общественной проблемой, а не с желанием съесть торт.

fixIt.text: The new government has promised to [[fight with]] corruption at every level.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Бороться с коррупцией» — combat (или fight) corruption, без with. Fight with someone значит «драться или ссориться с кем-то».

reply.context: At a residents' meeting, someone asks: "What is the council actually doing about all the graffiti?"
options: We're combating it by giving everyone free spray paint.
We're combating it with faster clean-ups and legal walls where artists can paint.
Yeah, we're kinda combating it, like, sort of.
reply.explanationRu: Combat — бороться с проблемой, чтобы её стало меньше, а бесплатная краска только добавит граффити. Третий ответ слишком небрежный для официальной встречи.

definitionEn: to begin or start, especially in official situations
situation: An official notice, contract or announcement says when work, a ceremony or a legal process will start.

examples.text: Construction of the new bridge will [[commence]] in early spring, subject to planning permission.
The ceremony will [[commence]] at 11 a.m., and guests are asked to be seated by 10.45.
Successful candidates will [[commence]] employment on 1 September.

texts: Boarding will [[commence]] thirty minutes before departure.
Please do not [[commence]] the exam until you are told to.
Repairs to the roof will [[commence]] once the rain stops.

badCollocation.noteRu: Commence — официальное слово. О бытовых делах говорят start или begin: start the washing-up.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Начать судебный процесс — commence (или start, bring) legal proceedings. Make, do и set с proceedings не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The anniversary celebrations will [[commence]] with a parade through the old town.
nuance.explanationRu: Commence — начинаться (официально). Commemorate — чтить память о событии или человеке, например commemorate the victims; начаться с парада им нельзя.

reverse.text: A statue was put up to [[commemorate]] the town's most famous poet.
reverse.explanationRu: Увековечить память — commemorate. Commence значит «начинать(ся)» и к памятнику не подходит.

fixIt.text: According to the official notice, the hearing will [[kick off]] at 10 a.m. in Courtroom 2.
fixIt.explanationRu: В официальном объявлении kick off звучит слишком разговорно. Здесь нужно формальное commence.

wordFormation.text: The [[commencement]] of the new contract has been delayed until June.

reply.context: At a formal conference, the chair turns to you and asks: "Is the panel ready to begin?"
options: Yes, we're ready to commence whenever you are.
Yes, we commenced an hour ago, so we're just about to start.
Yeah, let's get this show on the road, mate!
reply.explanationRu: Commence значит «начинать», поэтому «начали час назад и вот-вот начнём» — бессмыслица. Третий ответ слишком фамильярный для официальной конференции.

definitionEn: a live description of a match, race or ceremony for listeners or viewers
senseNote: Здесь — живой репортаж (football commentary); commentary также значит «комментарий к тексту» или «критический взгляд» (a commentary on modern life).
situation: Someone describes a football match, a race or a royal wedding live for people who are watching or listening.

examples.text: I prefer to watch the match with the sound off, because the [[commentary]] is so annoying.
We followed the race on the car radio, listening to the live [[commentary]] from the track.
My aunt kept up a running [[commentary]] on everything we passed during the drive.

texts: The [[commentary]] on tonight's final will be available in three languages.
You can switch off the [[commentary]] and just hear the crowd.
She has done the radio [[commentary]] for the marathon for twenty years.

badCollocation.noteRu: Комментарий под постом или статьёй — a comment: leave a comment. Commentary — репортаж или развёрнутый разбор.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Непрерывно комментировать происходящее — keep up a running commentary. Comment, report и speech с running в этом значении не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Millions of fans listened to the radio [[commentary]] as the final went into extra time.
nuance.explanationRu: Commentary — непрерывный репортаж о событии в эфире. Comment — отдельное замечание или реплика; радиорепортаж так не называют.

reverse.text: The minister refused to make any [[comment]] on the rumours.
reverse.explanationRu: Отдельное высказывание или заявление — comment: make a comment, no comment. Commentary — развёрнутый репортаж или разбор.

fixIt.text: The radio [[reportage]] of the match was so exciting that I forgot to eat.
fixIt.explanationRu: Репортаж о матче в прямом эфире — commentary. Reportage — журналистские материалы или фоторепортаж, о трансляции матча так не говорят.

wordFormation.text: The TV [[commentary]] was so biased that I switched over to the radio.

reply.context: A friend messages: "My TV's broken, so we'll have to follow the final on the radio. Still coming over?"
options: Of course! Radio commentary is actually more exciting — you imagine everything.
Sure! And afterwards we can read the commentary under the club's post.
I shall attend, provided the commentary is of an acceptable standard.
reply.explanationRu: Отзывы под постом — comments, а не commentary. Commentary — живой репортаж, как на радио. Третий ответ звучит чопорно и официально.

definitionEn: an expert who discusses news or events on TV, radio or in newspapers
senseNote: Здесь — эксперт, который обсуждает события в СМИ (a political commentator); в спорте commentator ещё и ведёт прямой репортаж.
situation: An expert appears on the news or writes in the press to explain and give opinions on current events.

examples.text: On election night, TV channels invited [[commentators]] to explain what the results meant.
According to several financial [[commentators]], house prices could fall sharply next year.
The former footballer now works as a TV [[commentator]], analysing matches after they finish.

texts: She is a respected [[commentator]] on Middle Eastern politics.
The [[commentator]] predicted a crisis that never came.
He's a regular [[commentator]] on the evening news.

badCollocation.noteRu: Спортивный комментатор — a sports commentator: в роли определения обычно sports с -s (sports news, sports car).

collocationTask.explanationRu: Эксперт по какой-то теме — a commentator on something: нужен предлог on. In, at и about в этом сочетании не используются.

nuance.text: The channel invited a [[commentator]] to explain the new tax rules to viewers.
nuance.explanationRu: Commentator — эксперт, которого приглашают в эфир или публикуют в газете. Commenter — любой, кто оставил комментарий в интернете.

reverse.text: One angry [[commenter]] wrote that the article was full of mistakes.
reverse.explanationRu: Автора комментария под статьёй называют commenter. Commentator — эксперт или ведущий репортажа в СМИ.

fixIt.text: The [[politologist]] on the evening news said the result was no surprise.
fixIt.explanationRu: Эксперта, который обсуждает политику в СМИ, называют political commentator или analyst. Слово politologist в английском почти не используется.

wordFormation.text: Some political [[commentators]] believe the new party could win seats next year.

reply.context: Your colleague says: "Did you see that economist on TV last night? She explained the budget really clearly."
options: Yes, she's a great commentator — she never gives her opinion on anything.
Affirmative. The commentator's discourse was of satisfactory quality.
Yes, she's one of the few commentators who actually make economics interesting.
reply.explanationRu: Commentator — эксперт, который как раз высказывает мнение о событиях. Второй ответ звучит как протокол или робот, а не разговор с коллегой.

definitionEn: the business of buying and selling goods and services, especially on a large scale
senseNote: У слова одно значение — торговля как сфера деятельности; для C1 важны сочетания e-commerce и the Chamber of Commerce.
situation: People talk about trade and business activity in general, such as online shopping or trade between countries.

examples.text: For centuries, the river was the main route for [[commerce]] between the coast and the interior.
The internet has transformed [[commerce]]: you can now buy almost anything without leaving home.
She is studying [[commerce]] and hopes to work in international banking.

texts: The Chamber of [[Commerce]] opposes the new parking charges.
Ports have always been centres of [[commerce]] and culture.
The minister for trade and [[commerce]] will visit the factory on Monday.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Заниматься коммерцией» — be in business или trade. Commerce — торговля как сфера, её не «делают».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Торговля и промышленность — commerce and industry. Commercial — прилагательное или рекламный ролик, merchandise — товары для продажи.

nuance.text: Most small shops now earn more from electronic [[commerce]] than from walk-in customers.
nuance.explanationRu: Commerce — торговля как сфера деятельности, отсюда устойчивое electronic commerce (e-commerce). Trade — обмен товарами, особенно между странами: foreign trade, a trade deal.

reverse.text: The two countries signed a new [[trade]] agreement last week.
reverse.explanationRu: Торговое соглашение между странами — trade agreement. Commerce в таких сочетаниях не используется.

fixIt.text: Cross-border [[commercial]] between the two countries doubled after the new bridge opened.
fixIt.explanationRu: Торговля — commerce. A commercial — рекламный ролик на ТВ или радио, а commercial как прилагательное значит «коммерческий».

wordFormation.text: The film was a huge [[commercial]] success but got terrible reviews.
